issues.legal_issue: The availability of a civil remedy does not by itself justify quashing a criminal complaint that prima facie alleges an offence.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that the accused had fraudulently induced the complainant’s father to execute a gift deed.
After a remand, the Magistrate issued process for alleged offences of cheating, forgery and conspiracy.
The High Court quashed the complaint because it considered the allegations to disclose a civil wrong and continuation of the prosecution to be an abuse of process.
The High Court did not find that the complaint’s allegations disclosed no offence.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not quash the complaint solely because the facts also gave rise to a civil claim. Its order was set aside and the trial court was directed to proceed with the complaint in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: A set of facts may give rise both to a civil claim and to criminal liability; the availability of a civil remedy does not preclude criminal prosecution where the alleged conduct also makes out an offence. The Court relied on Trisuns Chemical Industry v. Rajesh Agarwal, which held that even arbitration is not an effective substitute for criminal prosecution when the conduct also constitutes an offence. The inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure may be used to prevent abuse of process, but the complaint cannot be quashed merely because a civil remedy is available.

rule.if: criminal_complaint_proceeding and civil_claim_available and prima_facie_offence_alleged and not finding_that_allegations_disclose_no_offence

predicates.criminal_complaint_proceeding: A complainant has initiated a criminal proceeding alleging that another person committed an offence.
predicates.civil_claim_available: The alleged facts also provide a basis for pursuing a civil claim.
predicates.prima_facie_offence_alleged: The complaint’s allegations, at the preliminary stage, indicate conduct that may constitute an offence.
predicates.finding_that_allegations_disclose_no_off: The court has found that the complaint’s allegations do not disclose any offence.
predicates.civil_remedy_exists: A civil remedy is available in respect of the alleged conduct.

issues.definition: When a criminal complaint prima facie alleges an offence and the same facts also support a civil claim, the complaint is not to be quashed solely because a civil remedy exists.

issues.legal_issue: A criminal complaint may be quashed where its allegations do not disclose an offence, but the inherent power to quash cannot be used on that basis unless the complaint’s allegations support that conclusion.
material_facts: The accused sought quashing under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The High Court quashed the complaint on the ground that it disclosed a civil wrong, rather than finding that the allegations made out no offence.
The Supreme Court held that the complaint could not be treated as frivolous at the prima facie stage on the facts presented.
issues.conclusion: A complaint that does not disclose an offence may be quashed to prevent abuse of process, but that ground did not justify quashing this complaint because the High Court had not found that the allegations disclosed no offence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, inherent powers may be exercised to prevent abuse of the process of law and secure the ends of justice. Proceedings may be quashed where the allegations in a complaint or FIR do not constitute the alleged offence or disclose any offence. The Court relied on State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal and K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar for these principles.

predicates.criminal_complaint_proceeding: A complainant has initiated a criminal proceeding alleging that another person committed an offence.
predicates.complaint_allegations_do_not_disclose_of: The facts alleged in the complaint do not constitute or disclose an offence.

issues.definition: When a criminal complaint’s allegations do not disclose an offence, the complaint may be quashed to prevent abuse of process.
